stories.title: A framework for spatial modelling of potentials for vegetation development and associated land use in heterogeneous landscapes
stories.description: Understanding spatial variation in ecological opportunity is fundamental to predicting vegetation development and informing land-use planning, yet existing geoecological models are often constrained by categorical inputs, genesis-based classifications and dependence on current land use and vegetation patterns. Here we present a holistic, unsupervised framework for delineating geoecological land units and gradients using continuous environmental variables selected for high temporal permanence. The method integrates topographic, pedological, and hydrological factors through a grouped principal component analysis followed by multivariate clustering, enabling balanced representation of interacting ecological factors without predefined hierarchies. Applied at 10 m resolution in Eastern Denmark, the model identifies 16 geotope categories representing discrete, functional land unit types for vegetation development. Statistical validation shows that multivariate heterogeneity is concentrated at geotope boundaries, while interiors are internally more homogeneous. This indicates a robust delineation of patch–gradient landscape structure and validates the model design. The framework provides a scalable approach for mapping geoecological potentials relevant to conservation planning, vegetation modelling, land suitability assessment, opportunity mapping and land system analysis.

stories.title: Toward long-term stability of SAW sensor interface electronics with minimized heat generation and baseline fluctuation
stories.description: Three different interface architectures were developed to convert changes in surface acoustic wave (SAW) velocity, generated by a two-port SAW delay line with a UV-C sensing material, into measurable frequency shifts for real-time monitoring and analysis. The system includes an oscillator, multiplexer (MUX), mixer, low-pass filter (LPF), comparator, field-programmable gate array (FPGA), and a PC-based visualization unit. The three architectures were evaluated based on signal stability, noise performance, baseline drift, and frequency detection accuracy. All designs demonstrated low noise, minimal heat generation, and stable long-term operation with negligible baseline fluctuations. Depending on the specific sensor application, the most appropriate architecture can be selected and integrated into the system. Each architecture provides a compact and reliable solution for high-resolution SAW sensor signal processing and monitoring. Additionally, a visualization algorithm was implemented to display real-time data and provide warning alerts using color-coded indicators around the display window.

stories.title: Festivities at the edge of data: an interdisciplinary study of Andean festivals in wikidata
stories.description: This article examines how two Andean ritual traditions, Qoyllur Rit’i and the Virgen del Carmen of Paucartambo, are structurally represented within Wikidata. Using a compact knowledge graph extracted from Wikidata through ritual, geographic, heritage, and classificatory relations, we combine Louvain community detection, k-core coreness, and complementary network measures to analyze their relational embedding. The results show a tension between two forms of computational visibility. Qoyllur Rit’i is associated with a broader national-regional cluster but remains outside the innermost structural core, while the Virgen del Carmen of Paucartambo appears in a small ritual-specific community and occupies an outer core level. Institutional and geopolitical entities, together with heritage-classification entities, occupy the structural core of the graph. We interpret these patterns not as direct measures of cultural significance, but as evidence of how Wikidata’s semantic model, classification properties, linking practices, and editorial accumulation make some cultural relations more visible than others. The paper contributes to digital humanities and critical heritage studies by showing how graph analysis can serve as a diagnostic tool for examining the limits of linked open data in representing ritual practices, collective memory, and embodied forms of cultural knowledge.

stories.title: A comparative study of path planning algorithms for low-altitude emergency medical UAVs considering task priorities
stories.description: In urban emergency medical scenarios, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) path planning faces severe challenges from superimposed uncertain factors: dynamic emergency task insertions, sudden no-fly zones (NFZs), and day-to-night environmental transitions. While existing studies frequently address these issues in isolation, there remains a critical lack of systematic benchmarking frameworks that incorporate these stress factors simultaneously. Based on Guangzhou geographic data, this study constructs a medical network with 6 blood centers and 12 hospitals, designing six composite stress-testing scenarios. Seven algorithms spanning a three-tier capability gradient (exact MILP, metaheuristics MSHOA/ACO/GA/PSO, and learning-driven QALNS/PPO) are systematically evaluated across six performance dimensions. Results show MILP establishes the theoretical optimality bound (1 582 CNY) in baseline scenarios but fails to solve within 1 200 s under sudden NFZ constraints. MSHOA yields the best solution quality (1 648 CNY) in conventional settings, though performance deteriorates under high-frequency emergency insertions. Notably, PPO demonstrates exceptional robustness across all dynamic scenarios, achieving a 0.4 s replanning time and > 95% task satisfaction after 10 consecutive emergency insertions, exhibiting the strongest robustness under tested conditions. Conversely, ACO and GA path feasibility plummets (23.8% and 44.9%) upon NFZ activation, exposing limitations in knowledge transfer under coupled constraints. This study pioneers a comprehensive benchmarking framework, providing a quantitative decision-making basis for robust low-altitude medical network scheduling.
